title: Termwise surjective quasi-isomorphisms of simplicial abelian groups are trivial Kan fibrations
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of simplicial objects in the category of abelian groups [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]. For a simplicial abelian group $X$ let $s(X)$ be its associated chain complex, with $s(X)_n=X_n$ for $n\geq0$, $s(X)_n=0$ for $n<0$, and differential $\sum_{i=0}^n(-1)^id_i:X_n\to X_{n-1}$ for $n>0$, with the differential in degree $0$ equal to the zero map $X_0\to0$; $f$ induces a morphism of chain complexes $s(f):s(X)\to s(Y)$ [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]. Assume that $f_n:X_n\to Y_n$ is surjective for every $n\geq0$ and that $H_n(s(f))$ is an isomorphism for every $n$. Then the map of underlying simplicial sets [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] is a trivial Kan fibration.

proof.text: Put $C_X^r=s(X)_{-r}$ and $C_Y^r=s(Y)_{-r}$, with $d_{C_X}^r=d_{s(X),-r}$ and the analogous differential on $C_Y$. These are exactly the nonpositive cochain complexes in [lem-trf-simplicial-abelian-surjective-quasi-iso-boundary-lifting]. Indeed, in degree $-n$ the term is $X_n$ and the differential is the same alternating sum for $n>0$; in degree $0$ and in positive degrees it is zero. The quotient formulas in [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology] and [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] give $H^r(C_X)=H_{-r}(s(X))$ and $H^r(C_Y)=H_{-r}(s(Y))$: their kernels and images are literally those of the same two homomorphisms. The induced maps also agree, since both send the class of $x$ to the class of $f_{-r}(x)$. Thus $C_f$ is a quasi-isomorphism by the assumed homology isomorphisms; for $r>0$ both cohomology groups are zero.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-simplicial-abelian-surjective-quasi-iso-boundary-lifting] to the given simplicial abelian groups and the unchanged morphism $f$. Its degreewise surjectivity hypothesis is precisely the hypothesis on $f_n$, and Step 1 verifies its quasi-isomorphism hypothesis. Its statement supplies fillers of every boundary square for the underlying simplicial-set map, including degree $0$. In particular, the empty-boundary square of a vertex $y\in Y_0$ supplies a vertex over $y$; the remaining squares are exactly those for $n\geq1$ in [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration]. Hence the underlying map is a trivial Kan fibration.
